comment: Versioned strategy parameters. Every assessment stores a hash of this file so Phase 3 can answer 'which thresholds produced this verdict?'. Change values via git commits, never ad hoc.

ingestion.venuesComment: Which programs to logsSubscribe to. This is the single biggest cost lever in the system: Helius meters websockets at 20 credits/MB and logsSubscribe delivers every transaction touching a program, of which we use well under 1%. Measured 2026-08-16: PumpSwap 104 GB/day (62M credits/month), pump.fun 13.5 GB/day (8.1M/month), against tiers of 1M free / 10M at $49 / 100M at $499. The full set exhausted a free allowance in ~10 hours. INGEST_PROFILE in .env overrides these unless it is set to custom. Defaults here are the developer-tier set; graduations are still detected with pumpswap off because migration transactions mention pump.fun as well.
ingestion.comment: pump.fun raw launches (~tens of thousands/day) are recorded but not snapshotted/filtered — graduation to PumpSwap is the quality gate that earns the full treatment. Flip a source between lists to change policy.

snapshots.comment: Decaying cadence: dense where the action is (first minutes), sparse later. `schedule` drives price/liquidity, which come from one batched Jupiter request covering every tracked mint and cost no RPC credits. `chainStateAtSec` (authorities + concentration, 2 RPC calls) and `holdersAtSec` (1 DAS call) are per-mint and metered, so they only refresh at these ages and are carried forward in between with their real observation timestamps. holdersAtSec does NOT start at 0, and 60s was measured to be too early too: a freshly observed mint reported 2 holders at t=0 against 1404 ten minutes later, and at 60s three tokens read 7, 9 and 1 against 167, 57 and 70 roughly a minute afterwards. The count is still converging that early, so judging minHolders against it rejects tokens for an artifact. 180s is the first age we are willing to decide on; minHolders was MEASURED against recorded distributions on 2026-08-17 and 180s is vindicated: of 105 paired mints reading under 50 holders at 3 min that also had a 10 min read, only 2 reached 50 by 10 min, and of the 16 reading exactly 0 at 3 min, ZERO climbed above 0. So the low group is genuinely sparse, not still-converging -- the bar rejects dead tokens, not an artifact. First-read distribution over 552 mints: p10 6, p25 18, median 167, p75 446, p90 707; 31% fall under the pass bar of 50 and 45% under the notify bar of 175 -- but of the 485 mints with all three notify fields, LIQUIDITY binds far harder: 90% fail minLiquidityUsd 30000, 58% fail top10, 45% fail holders, and holders is the SOLE failure for only 3%. Alert volume is governed by liquidity, not holders. The medians grow overall (178 -> 292 across the paired subset), but that growth is concentrated in tokens that already had traction at 3 min. Holder counts saturate at 3000 (DAS 3 pages x 1000) and snapshots now record holder_count_truncated so a ceiling is not read as a count; 5 of 552 mints are affected, all far above these floors. Horizon cut 3600 -> 1800 on 2026-08-16: at ~110 new tokens/hour the old cadence implied ~9.3M RPC calls/month against a 1M/month allowance.

swaps.comment: Swap recording feeds H1, which is stated as unique-buyer growth without wash signatures. Per-minute buckets run for the whole tracking window; raw per-swap rows are kept only inside the launch windows, because tracked-token swaps measured 7.1M/day and storing them all would dwarf the dataset. These four numbers are the volume dials: measured trades within 20 slots of a pump.fun launch run mean 18.7 / median 8 / p90 35 / max 194, so maxRawPerToken trims a long tail without touching the typical case. Re-measure real growth after 24h before widening anything.

quotes.comment: Execution-cost sampling (FR-A6), feeding FR-B3's expectancy-net-of-costs. sizeSol is the standard trade the whole dataset is denominated in -- changing it changes what every previously recorded cost means, so treat it as a breaking change, not a tweak. exitHorizonsMin re-prices the same position later; FR-B3 models exit cost as entry impact x2, and these rows let Phase 3 check that assumption against reality instead of inheriting it.

meta.comment: FR-J1 regime thermometer. Every rate is PER COVERED HOUR, never per day: ingest duty-cycles by design (the 2 GB/day byte ceiling stops a developer-profile pump.fun stream after ~3.6 of every 24 hours) and stops entirely when the allowance runs out, so a daily count cannot tell a quiet market from a blind recorder. minCoveredHours is an absolute floor below which no rate is claimed -- deliberately NOT a percentage of the day, which at a 15% designed duty cycle would leave the gauge permanently UNKNOWN. cohortMinAgeHours removes the other bias: a token launched at 20:00 cannot graduate before midnight, so the graduation rate that votes is measured only over launches old enough to have had a fair chance. Bands are anchored on 2026-08-16, the only day measured: 5.5 covered hours carried 10,136 pump.fun launches (~1,850/h), 15,315 PumpSwap SOL (~2,800/h) and a 1.2% same-day graduation ratio -- so the seeded NORMAL band is centred on that one day of one regime. These carry NO outcome evidence; they are a first calibration to be re-fitted in Phase 3 against FR-B4, exactly like the notify bar. COLD suppresses Telegram delivery only -- recording never depends on the regime. UNKNOWN does not suppress (operator decision, 2026-08-16): only positive evidence of COLD silences the channel, never the gauge being blind.

alerts.comment: The `thresholds` block decides what PASSES and is therefore what the dataset records: every pass gets an alerts row and FR-A6 cost quotes. This `notify` block decides only what reaches Telegram. They are deliberately separate, because alert volume is also the execution-cost sampling rate -- tightening the pass bar to quieten the phone would cut the cost dataset by the same factor, and marginal candidates are exactly the ones that teach you where the liquidity cliff is. Measured 2026-08-16 over 485 mints: the pass bar yields ~415 alerts/day, this notify bar ~52/day. These numbers come from ~4 hours of one market regime and carry NO outcome evidence -- they are a capacity choice about how many messages are readable, not a claim about expectancy. Revisit in Phase 3 against real outcomes (FR-B4).
